skill.name: amazon-product-api-skill
skill.description: Extract structured Amazon product listing data through the BrowserAct Amazon Product API template. The skill accepts search keywords, brand filters, page count, and language settings for ecommerce research.
skill.summary: Extract Amazon listing data with a BrowserAct workflow.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally calls BrowserAct external workflow APIs and handles a BrowserAct API key. Most markdown backtick and system reconnaissance alerts are false positives, but credential handling, chat-based key solicitation, and anti-bot claims remain material concerns. Publication should wait until secret handling and compliance guidance are corrected.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs users to provide BROWSERACT_API_KEY in chat.
remediation.suggestion: Require environment variables or approved secret storage only, and remove any instruction to paste API keys into conversation.

remediation.issue: The skill sends authenticated requests and search parameters to BrowserAct.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact external endpoint, data sent, retention expectations, and consent requirements before execution.

remediation.issue: The documentation advertises avoiding captcha and IP restrictions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove circumvention language and add clear guidance about site terms, lawful collection, and rate limits.

remediation.issue: The markdown command example relies on shell-style argument passing.
remediation.suggestion: Provide safer invocation guidance that quotes user inputs and avoids shell interpolation of untrusted text.

content.user_title: Extract Amazon Product Data with BrowserAct
content.value_statement: Manual Amazon product research is slow and hard to compare. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow to collect listings, prices, ratings, ASINs, and attributes.
actual_capabilities: Runs the BrowserAct Amazon Product API template with keywords, brand, page count, and language inputs.
Reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment before making API requests.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow and polls task status with timestamped progress logs.
Requests Amazon listing fields such as title, ASIN, product URL, brand, price, and rating.
Reports missing or invalid API key conditions with user-facing error messages.
Supports localized Amazon browsing by passing a language parameter.
limitations: Requires a valid BrowserAct API key and sends requests to BrowserAct servers.
Current script control flow may return a timeout before result retrieval runs.
Depends on BrowserAct and Amazon availability, not local browser scraping.
Users must confirm that collection follows site terms, laws, and rate limits.

use_cases.title: Compare Product Listings
use_cases.description: Collect Amazon listings for a category and compare prices, ratings, and featured badges.

use_cases.title: Track Competitor Pricing
use_cases.description: Review current Amazon prices for a specific competitor brand and identify discount patterns.

use_cases.title: Enrich Product Records
use_cases.description: Gather ASINs, product URLs, attributes, and ratings for catalog maintenance workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Product Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for one brand and one page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Amazon products for 'wireless earbuds' from Samsung. Use one page and English language. Return titles, ASINs, prices, ratings, and links.

prompt_templates.title: Brand Price Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare pricing and ratings for one competitor.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Amazon for laptops from Dell and summarize pricing, ratings, and featured badges. Highlight products with strong rating counts.

prompt_templates.title: Localized Market Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a non-English Amazon browsing session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Amazon for coffee makers using German language settings. Focus on Philips products across two pages and summarize notable price ranges.

prompt_templates.title: Structured Market Dataset
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced collection for downstream pricing analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect Amazon listing data for ergonomic office chairs across three pages. Organize results for pricing analysis, including ASINs, ratings, badges, and attributes.

output_examples.input: Search wireless earbuds for Samsung on one page.
output_examples.output: A ranked product list with title, ASIN, current price, original price when available, rating, rating count, badge, and product link.

output_examples.input: Compare Dell laptops across two result pages.
output_examples.output: A comparison summary grouped by price bands, with high-rating products and visible discount signals called out.

output_examples.input: Find German-language Philips coffee maker listings.
output_examples.output: Localized listing details with product names, ASINs, prices, ratings, and attributes available from the BrowserAct workflow.

best_practices: Store BrowserAct credentials in environment variables or approved secret storage.
Use narrow keywords and brand filters to reduce unnecessary external requests.
Review Amazon terms, rate limits, and privacy requirements before collecting data.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into chat or shared transcripts.
Do not use broad scraping prompts that ignore site rules or rate limits.
Do not treat missing fields as confirmed absence from Amazon listings.

faq.question: Does this skill need a BrowserAct API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment and cannot run without valid credentials.

faq.question: Does it scrape Amazon directly from my machine?
faq.answer: No. It starts a BrowserAct workflow through the BrowserAct API.

faq.question: What data can it request?
faq.answer: It can request titles, ASINs, product URLs, brands, prices, ratings, badges, and selected attributes.

faq.question: Can it monitor prices over time?
faq.answer: It can collect current listing data. Scheduled monitoring requires separate automation outside this skill.

faq.question: Can I use non-English Amazon sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts a language value such as en, de, or zh-CN.

faq.question: Are there security concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. Keep API keys out of chat and review external data sharing before use.
